Retrieves file content. Returns raw binary file data when Accept header is set to application/octet-stream,

post.description:
Creates a message using Anthropic Messages API format.
Supports streaming via SSE.

**Async inference:** Send `x-bf-async: true` to submit the request as a background job and receive a job ID immediately. Poll with `x-bf-async-id: <job-id>` to retrieve the result. When the job is still processing, the response will have an empty `content` array. When completed, `content` will contain the full result. See [Async Inference](/features/async-inference) for details.

parameters.name: x-bf-async
parameters.description: Set to `true` to submit this request as an async job. Returns immediately with a job ID. Not compatible with streaming.

parameters.name: x-bf-async-id
parameters.description: Poll for results of a previously submitted async job by providing the job ID returned from the initial async request.

parameters.name: x-bf-async-job-result-ttl
parameters.description: Override the default result TTL in seconds. Results expire after this duration from completion time.

get.description:
Retrieves CADF-compliant audit log events with filtering, search, and
pagination via query parameters. Most filter dimensions accept either a
single value (singular parameter, e.g. `action`) or a JSON-encoded array
of values (plural parameter, e.g. `actions`); when both are supplied the
plural array takes precedence.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of events to return per page (default 100, max 1000).

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free-text search across audit event fields.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Filter by a single CADF action.

parameters.name: actions
parameters.description: JSON array of CADF actions to filter by (OR match).

parameters.name: outcomes
parameters.description: JSON array of outcomes to filter by (OR match).

parameters.name: event_type
parameters.description: Filter by a single event type.

parameters.name: event_types
parameters.description: JSON array of event types to filter by (OR match).

parameters.name: initiator_id
parameters.description: Filter by a single initiator ID.

parameters.name: initiator_ids
parameters.description: JSON array of initiator IDs to filter by (OR match).

parameters.name: initiator_type
parameters.description: Filter by a single initiator resource type.

parameters.name: initiator_types
parameters.description: JSON array of initiator resource types to filter by (OR match).

parameters.name: target_id
parameters.description: Filter by a single target ID.

parameters.name: target_ids
parameters.description: JSON array of target IDs to filter by (OR match).

parameters.name: target_type
parameters.description: Filter by a single target resource type.

parameters.name: target_types
parameters.description: JSON array of target resource types to filter by (OR match).

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: Filter events at or after this time (RFC3339 or `YYYY-MM-DD`).

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: Filter events at or before this time (RFC3339 or `YYYY-MM-DD`; a date is treated as end-of-day).

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: Relative time window that overrides `start_date`/`end_date` when set (e.g. `24h`, `7d`).

parameters.name: request_method
parameters.description: Filter by a single HTTP request method.

parameters.name: request_methods
parameters.description: JSON array of HTTP request methods to filter by (OR match).

parameters.name: request_path
parameters.description: Filter by a single request path prefix.

parameters.name: request_paths
parameters.description: JSON array of request path prefixes to filter by (OR match).

parameters.name: request_ip
parameters.description: Filter by a single client IP address.

parameters.name: request_ips
parameters.description: JSON array of client IP addresses to filter by (OR match).

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: JSON array of tags to filter by (any match).

get.description:
Streams audit log events matching the supplied filters as a downloadable
file. Accepts the same filter query parameters as `GET /api/audit-logs`.
The response is returned as an attachment with a generated filename.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description:
Export format. Defaults to `json` when omitted or unrecognized.
- `json`: a JSON array of events
- `jsonl`: JSON Lines, one event per line
- `syslog`: RFC 5424 syslog format

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free-text search across audit event fields.

parameters.name: actions
parameters.description: JSON array of CADF actions to filter by (OR match).

parameters.name: outcomes
parameters.description: JSON array of outcomes to filter by (OR match).

parameters.name: event_types
parameters.description: JSON array of event types to filter by (OR match).

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: Filter events at or after this time (RFC3339 or `YYYY-MM-DD`).

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: Filter events at or before this time (RFC3339 or `YYYY-MM-DD`).

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: Relative time window that overrides `start_date`/`end_date` when set (e.g. `24h`, `7d`).

200.description: A streamed export of the matching audit logs.

get.description:
Returns the distinct values available for each audit log filter dimension,
used to populate filter dropdowns in the dashboard.

parameters.name: dimensions
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of dimensions to return. When omitted, all
dimensions are returned. Unknown dimensions are ignored.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Optional case-insensitive substring filter applied to dimension values.

get.description: Retrieves a single audit log event by its unique ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the audit log event.

get.description:
Recomputes the HMAC-SHA256 signature for a single audit log event and
compares it (in constant time) against the stored signature to detect
tampering.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the audit log event to verify.

get.description:
Returns the method-B registry: alias token → customer or team. Requires
the `ldap.read` permission at global scope.

Each filter accepts a comma-separated list and may also be repeated; values within a field are OR-ed, different fields are AND-ed.

parameters.name: scope_type
parameters.description: Filter by scope type(s), comma-separated or repeated. An unrecognized value is a 400.

parameters.name: scope_id
parameters.description: Filter by customer/team ID(s), comma-separated or repeated.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort column. An unrecognized value falls back to `created_at` rather than failing the request.

post.description:
Registers an alias token for a customer or team, so directory attribute
values can name Meridian scopes without carrying opaque IDs. Requires
`ldap.manage` at global scope.

409.description: The alias token is already registered

503.description: The LDAP store is not initialized on this node

put.description:
Repoints the alias at a different scope, or renames it. Same validation as
create. Requires `ldap.manage` at global scope.

409.description: Another alias already uses that token

503.description: The LDAP store is not initialized on this node

delete.description:
Deletes the alias. Directory values referencing it are skipped from the
next sync tick onward (counted as `values_skipped`). Requires
`ldap.manage` at global scope.

get.description:
Returns the method-A rules: LDAP group DN → role at a scope. Requires the
`ldap.read` permission at global scope.

Each filter accepts a comma-separated list and may also be repeated; values within a field are OR-ed, different fields are AND-ed.

parameters.name: role_name
parameters.description: Filter by role name(s), comma-separated or repeated.

parameters.name: scope_type
parameters.description: Filter by scope type(s), comma-separated or repeated. An unrecognized value is a 400.

parameters.name: scope_id
parameters.description: Filter by customer/team ID(s), comma-separated or repeated.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort column. An unrecognized value falls back to `created_at` rather than failing the request.

post.description:
Creates a method-A rule. The role must exist and be bindable at the given
scope type, and the scope must name an existing customer or team; the
group DN is lowercased before storage. Requires `ldap.manage` at global
scope.

The rule is NOT applied on write — the next sync tick reads the registry
fresh and reconciles bindings then.

409.description: A rule with the same (group_dn, role, scope) tuple already exists

503.description: The LDAP store is not initialized on this node

put.description:
Replaces the rule's group DN, role and scope. Same validation as create.
Requires `ldap.manage` at global scope.

409.description: The update would collide with another rule's (group_dn, role, scope) tuple

503.description: The LDAP store is not initialized on this node

delete.description:
Deletes the rule. Bindings it previously produced are removed by the next
sync tick, not by this call. Requires `ldap.manage` at global scope.

get.summary: LDAP integration status and sync state
get.description:
Returns whether the directory integration is enabled, the directory's host,
and the sync engine's observable state with the last tick's counters.
Requires the `ldap.read` permission at global scope.

The response is deliberately narrow: the service-account DN and its
password are never echoed, and the configured URL is reduced to its host.

post.description:
Runs a directory sweep immediately instead of waiting for the next tick.
Requires `ldap.manage` at global scope.

The run is asynchronous: `202` means accepted, not finished — poll
`GET /api/auth/ldap/status` for the outcome. Only the meta leader writes
users and bindings, so a request that lands on a follower is forwarded to
the leader and its answer relayed verbatim; `502` reports a leader that
could not be reached. `409 not the meta leader` is reachable only when no
leader can be named, or when the request already crossed one hop.

202.description: Sync accepted and scheduled

409.description: Refused — a tick is already running, the provider is disabled, the engine is shutting down, or this node is not the leader and the leader could not be named (forwarding answers every other follower case). Every refusal uses this one body shape.

502.description: This node is not the meta leader and the leader could not be reached — the dial or its DNS resolution failed. Distinct from `409`: the leader did not refuse, it was never asked. Forwarding composes the leader's address from its node name, so this is what a node id that is not resolvable, or a cluster with non-uniform HTTP ports, answers.

503.description: The sync engine is not initialized on this node

get.description:
Returns the directory synchronization run history: why a run failed, which
directory values were skipped and which accounts changed. Requires the
`ldap.read` permission at global scope.

`GET /api/auth/ldap/status` reports only the CURRENT state — one row that every
tick overwrites. This endpoint is the history behind it.

Which events exist at all depends on the configured `sync_log_level`
(`off` | `error` | `warn` | `info`, default `warn`): at the default level a healthy
run writes nothing, so an empty log is the normal steady state rather than a fault.

Each filter accepts a comma-separated list and may also be repeated; values within a field are OR-ed, different fields are AND-ed.

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: Filter by severity level(s), comma-separated or repeated. A value naming no level simply matches nothing.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Filter by event code(s), comma-separated or repeated.

parameters.name: run_id
parameters.description: Return only events from one sync run.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Lower bound on `created_at`, inclusive. RFC3339; an unparseable value is a 400.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Upper bound on `created_at`, inclusive. RFC3339; an unparseable value is a 400.

200.description: Successful response. Events are ordered newest first.

get.description:
Returns a paged list of authorization audit records. Requires the
audit-log list permission (any global-scope binding). Usernames are
enriched app-side.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on the record timestamp (RFC3339). Mutually exclusive with `relative`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Inclusive upper bound on the record timestamp (RFC3339). Mutually exclusive with `relative`.

parameters.name: relative
parameters.description:
Trailing time window evaluated at request time: the server expands it to
[now − duration, now]. Accepts Go duration syntax (5m, 30m, 1h, 24h) plus
a `d` suffix for days (2d, 7d, 30d). Mutually exclusive with `from`/`to` (400).

parameters.name: permission
parameters.description: Comma-separated permission names; matches records for ANY of them.

parameters.name: scope_type
parameters.description: Comma-separated scope types; matches records at ANY of them.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description: Plain substring match on the resource (no wildcard syntax — LIKE metacharacters are escaped).

get.description:
Returns a paged list of scoped role bindings ("user U holds role R at scope
(type, id)"). Requires the rbac.binding.list permission.

The `user_id`, `role_name`, `scope_type` and `source` filters accept
comma-separated lists matched with IN semantics. `customer_id` and `team_id` are
comma-separated scope-pair filters matching bindings at scope
(customer, id) / (team, id) respectively; they combine as one OR group
ANDed with the remaining filters.

Results are filtered by the caller's visibility: callers with global
visibility (legacy admin, a global binding, or auth-disabled deployments)
see every binding; scoped callers see only bindings at their visible
scopes plus teams under their visible customers.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: Filter by grantee user ID(s), comma-separated

parameters.name: customer_id
parameters.description: Filter to bindings at scope (customer, id) for these customer ID(s), comma-separated

parameters.name: team_id
parameters.description: Filter to bindings at scope (team, id) for these team ID(s), comma-separated

parameters.name: scope_id
parameters.description: Exact scope ID match (legacy single-value filter)

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Filter by binding provenance(s), comma-separated: `manual` (granted through this API) or `ldap` (written by the directory sync)

post.description:
Grants a user a built-in role at a scope. The role must be bindable at the
requested scope type, the global scope requires an empty scope_id, and both
the user and the scope entity must exist. created_by is set to the
requestor.

Anti-escalation subset rule: the caller must be admin-classified at the
binding's scope or a covering ancestor (global admin → anything; customer
admin → own customer and its teams; team admin → own team only), otherwise
403. Semantically duplicate grants — the same (user, role) already bound
at the same or a covering scope — are rejected with 409.

403.description: Forbidden - caller is not admin-classified at the binding's scope

409.description: Conflict - binding already exists (exact or subsumed by a covering scope)

delete.description:
Revokes a role binding by ID. The same anti-escalation subset rule as
binding creation applies (403 when the caller is not admin-classified at
the binding's scope). The bootstrap admin user's global-admin binding is
protected and cannot be removed (403).

403.description: Forbidden - subset rule, or the binding is the protected global-admin grant of the admin user

get.description:
Returns the authenticated caller's identity, legacy role, and every scoped
binding they hold — each enriched with its scope display name and the
per-scope effective permission names. Self-service — no permission
required; every logged-in user sees their own record.

Returns all role definitions with their permissions and assigned users.
Requires RBAC:View permission.

Returns the built-in ReBAC role catalog: each role's description, the scope
types it may be bound at, and its effective permission names per scope type.
Self-service — no permission required. The catalog is static build-time
metadata carrying no tenant data, and a scoped admin needs it to render the
role picker when granting a binding.

get.summary: Get another user's roles and bindings
get.description:
Returns the named user's identity, legacy role, and every scoped binding
they hold — the same document `/api/auth/rbac/me` returns for the caller.
Readable by any authenticated caller: the Users directory links each row
here, and a scoped caller has no other way to see who holds what. Note that
the response discloses the target's COMPLETE binding set, including bindings
at scopes the caller cannot otherwise see.

get.summary: List visible scopes of the caller
get.description:
Returns the authenticated caller's visible-scope set: the scopes they may
read (get/list) with an access classification. Access type is `admin` for
scopes where the caller holds an *.admin role and `viewer` otherwise.
Contains direct binding scopes only (no descendant expansion); a legacy
admin identity (or auth-disabled deployment) yields the single
global/admin entry. Self-service endpoint — no permission required.

Returns the UI-shell bootstrap payload: store-connectivity flags, an
access summary for the current caller (legacy role + whether they hold any
visible scope), and the configured support contacts. Self-service — any
authenticated user may call it; when authentication is disabled the caller
is treated as fully privileged (`has_any_access: true`). The access
summary is computed fail-closed: an error deriving visible scopes yields
500, never a fabricated grant.

delete.description: Clears a cache entry by its direct cache key.

delete.summary: Clear cache entry by cache ID
delete.description:
Deletes a single cache entry by its storage ID. Read the cache ID from
`extra_fields.cache_debug.cache_id` on a prior response — it is populated
on both cache hits and cache misses.

parameters.name: cacheId
parameters.description: Storage ID of the cache entry to delete

post.description:
Forces every shard's BudgetSyncer to run immediately, and returns the count
of shards whose trigger channel was signalled. Used by tests and incident
recovery to avoid waiting for the periodic ticker.

Requires the governance plugin to be loaded; otherwise 503.

shards_triggered.description: Number of shards whose sync was triggered

503.description: Governance plugin not loaded

get.summary: List this node's resilience event journal
get.description:
Pages the node-local resilience event journal newest-first: raft leadership
changes, quorum lost/achieved transitions, and gossip liveness edges, as
observed by THIS node (timestamps are the observer's local clock; entries
are never merged across nodes).

The journal is node-local and deliberately not topology-gated, so it keeps
answering while the cluster has lost quorum. A node without a journal
(single-node or community build) answers an empty page rather than an error.

parameters.name: before_seq
parameters.description:
Keyset cursor: return events with seq strictly below this value.
0 or absent starts at the newest event.

200.description: One page of the journal, newest first

node.description: The answering node — the observer this timeline belongs to.

at.description: Observation time on this node's local clock.

group.description: Raft group the event concerns (`_meta`, `shard0`, …); absent for liveness events.

node.description: Subject node of a liveness event.

healthy_voters.description: Healthy voter count at the quorum transition; null while unknown.

400.description: Malformed before_seq or limit, or a `shardLeader:` target with no shard id

post.summary: Promote this node to a single-node cluster (force-new)
post.description:
Arms an irreversible force-new-cluster rewrite on THIS node and gracefully
restarts the process into it: the survivor becomes the sole `_meta` voter,
every other node is marked excluded, and each group's replicas shrink to
the survivor's own. The break-glass recovery for a cluster whose quorum is
permanently lost — the other nodes must be dead, not partitioned.

Identity-confirmed and precondition-gated: `node_name`/`cluster_id` must
match the handling node, `confirm` must repeat the node name, `_meta` must
have observably lost quorum, every other voter must have been gossip-dead
for the configured minimum, every group must keep at least one replica on
the survivor, and no arm may already be pending. Failed preconditions are
collected into a 409 with machine-readable reasons. Accepts no dry-run
flag in the body or query — there is no preview for a restart.

node_name.description: Must name the node handling the request (the survivor).

cluster_id.description: Must match the node's cluster ID.

202.description: Armed; the process is restarting into the sole-voter rewrite

400.description: Malformed body, or a dry-run/apply flag in the body or query

409.description: Preconditions not met, or a promotion is already armed

503.description: The topology meta group is not available on this node

patch.description:
Flips an existing replica between voter and learner: `voter` promotes a
learner, `learner` demotes a voter. Group-scoped (`group_id` is a shard ID
or the reserved `_meta`), so it is uniform for the control plane.
Quorum-safety gated — a demote may not drop the group below quorum — and
idempotent when the replica already holds the role.

Adds and removes are NOT done here: replica membership is
placement-rule-driven, so there is no route for them at all.

This is the same declarative Plan/Apply flow as node and placement edits.
Promotion always waits for the learner to catch up before it becomes a
voter. Demotion transfers leadership first when necessary. `apply=false`
is a completely inert Latest-only stage. The same rules apply to data
groups and `_meta`.

parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description: A shard ID, or the reserved `_meta`

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name of the node hosting the replica

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The topology version the caller believes is current (compare-and-swap).

parameters.name: dry_run
parameters.description: Preview only — validate, commit nothing. Overridable in the body.

parameters.name: apply
parameters.description: After committing, reconcile now (true) or stage inertly (false). Overridable in the body.

200.description: Dry-run preview or inert Latest-only staged commit

202.description: Role target committed and asynchronous execution durably started

400.description:
An invalid `role`, an unparseable switch, or a quorum-safety refusal
(the demote would drop the group below quorum).

404.description: No such group, or the group has no replica on that node

412.description: `If-Match` is stale — re-read the current version and retry

421.description: This node does not lead the meta group — retry against the meta leader

503.description: Topology management is not active on this node, or the meta group has no quorum

post.summary: Reseat a replica under a fresh replica ID
post.description:
Re-declares one node's replica of a group under a FRESH replica ID. This is
the operator remedy for a replica whose node-local raft store is gone —
`GET /api/cluster/v1/status` reports it in `local_shards[]` with a
`parked_*` state.

A replica that has voted can never restart empty under the same ID (raft
would lose its vote and could elect two leaders for one term), and the
auto-repair reconciler will not heal it while raft still lists the ID in
the group's ConfState. Reseating retires the old identity and declares a
fresh one on the SAME node with the SAME role.

202, not 200: the document commit is synchronous, but convergence — remove
the old replica, clean its node-local state, add the fresh one as a learner
and promote it once caught up — runs asynchronously. Poll
`GET /api/cluster/v1/topology/executions/{id}` to follow it.

Takes no `If-Match`: the repair is committed atomically WITH its execution
authorization in one `_meta` proposal, and the server refuses outright
(409) unless Latest, Target and Active already agree and no execution is
running — a stricter precondition than a version compare-and-swap.

parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description: A shard ID. `_meta` is refused — the control plane is not reseatable.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name of the node hosting the replica

202.description: Fresh identity committed and asynchronous convergence durably started

400.description: `_meta` was named, or the replica is a learner rather than a voter

404.description: The topology declares no such group

409.description:
The cluster is mid-change — Latest, Target and Active disagree, or an
execution is still running. Retry once it converges.

412.description: The group declares no replica on that node

421.description: This node does not lead the meta group — retry against the meta leader

503.description: Topology management is not active on this node (no `_meta` group), or the meta group has no quorum

post.description:
Moves a raft group's leadership. Group-scoped, so it covers both a data
shard and the `_meta` control plane.

This is the one IMMEDIATE operation in v1: it commits no document and takes
no `If-Match`, because leadership is not declared state — the Document
never says who leads, raft decides, and an election can move it at any
moment.

202, not 200: raft applies the transfer asynchronously, so a success here
means "asked for", not "moved" — poll `GET /api/cluster/v1/status` for the
observed leader.

Omitting `target` auto-picks a voter of the group that is not the observed
leader and sits on an active node; a draining node is never chosen.

parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description: A shard ID, or the reserved `_meta`

requestBody.description: Optional — an omitted or empty `target` is auto-picked.

target.description: Node to move leadership to. Empty auto-picks an eligible voter.

202.description: Transfer initiated

target.description: The node leadership was asked to move to, whether named or auto-picked.

400.description: The group has no other active voter to transfer to — name a target explicitly

503.description:
Topology management is not active on this node, or the group has no
coordinator (static/community mode).

get.description:
Lists migrations newest first, optionally filtered to one customer, one
shard, or both (the filters are combined with AND).

Terminal history is retained for 30 days, so the listing is paged: `limit`
is clamped to 200 and the applied page bounds are echoed in the response.
Filter server-side rather than scanning the page: once 200 newer rows
exist, a client-side scan reads a truncated page as an empty result.

parameters.name: customer_id
parameters.description: Restrict the listing to one customer

parameters.name: shard_id
parameters.description: Restrict the listing to migrations involving one shard, as either the source or the destination

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size; 0 or above the maximum is clamped to 200

501.description: Customer migration is not available on this node

post.summary: Migrate a customer to another shard
post.description:
Starts a customer migration. The customer is the only supported migration
unit; teams and customer-direct virtual keys are internal fan-out groups.

Rejected with 400 for the default customer (`comm01`), for a destination
equal to the current shard, and for an undeclared destination shard. A
customer already carrying a non-terminal migration answers 409. Nodes
without PostgreSQL sharding (SQLite/community) answer 501.

400.description: Invalid customer, destination, or same-shard request

at `snapshotted`: past it the destination already holds imported budgets
that no proposal removes, so a later phase answers 409. An already-aborted
or failed migration answers 200 (idempotent); a committed one answers 409.

`force=true` widens the window to `applied`. The forced abort releases the
source fence and marks the record terminal without cleaning the destination
synchronously, so budget keys exist on both shards until the reconciler
reclaims them and enforcement is briefly imprecise. It is the short-MTTR
exit for a wedged migration; `retry` is the forward one.

already flipped the customer's shard assignment to the destination and no
abort path restores it, so a forced abort there would record a backward exit
for a move that in fact completed. Recover forward with `retry`, or move the
customer back with a fresh migration.

Returns the overall budget and rate limit quota for the authenticated virtual key,
as well as per-provider and per-model budgets and rate limits (with current usage).
Each budget also carries the actual per-model usage for its current cycle.

put.description:
Sets or replaces the spending override on one of a virtual key's budgets. The override is additive —
while it is active the budget is enforced against `max_limit + override_amount` — and it leaves the
budget's base limit, current usage, and reset schedule untouched.

Use `mode: cycles` with a `cycles` count to grant extra spend for a finite number of reset windows
(the current window counts as the first), or `mode: forever` to keep the override until it is deleted.
A finite grant is anchored to the budget's current reset window, so every node in a cluster derives the
same number of remaining cycles and a config reload cannot resurrect a spent one.

Removes any active override from the budget, so it is enforced against its base `max_limit` again.
The budget's current usage and reset schedule are unchanged, and the removal is permanent — a cleared
grant cannot be re-derived. Safe to call on a budget that has no override.

Hard-deletes a per-user-headers credential row by primary key. Authorization
scoping is enforced server-side — callers may only delete credentials
visible to their identity.

point; this typed endpoint exists for callers that already know they're
acting on a header credential row.

(required header names + optional admin header names). Used by the
`/workspace/mcp-sessions/auth?flow=<id>&kind=headers` landing page to
render the values form.

Requires management API authentication via `Authorization: Bearer <API key>`.

put.description:
Consumes a pending submission flow row: verifies the caller's values
against the upstream MCP server, upserts the credential keyed by the flow
row's (mode, identity), then deletes the flow row and the bound temp
token. Mirrors the OAuth callback's "complete the flow" semantics.

Values for any key not in the live `per_user_header_keys` schema are
dropped server-side so a stale UI can't persist deprecated keys.

422.description: Upstream verification failed with the supplied values

get.description:
Returns every per-user MCP authentication artifact visible to the caller —
OAuth tokens, header credentials, and pending submission / consent flows.

Row visibility is scoped to the caller's identity (Virtual Key, signed-in
user, or asserted session ID). Server-level `headers` / `oauth` clients
are not surfaced here; their credentials live on the MCP client config.

When both a credential and a pending flow exist for the same
`(identity, mcp_client)` binding, the credential is returned and the
flow is suppressed to avoid duplicate entries.

delete.description:
Revokes a session by primary key. Accepts these row kinds:
- OAuth token rows → hard-deletes the token plus any pending OAuth flow
  for the same binding (so an in-flight callback can't undo the revoke)
- Header credential rows → hard-deletes the credential plus any pending
  header submission flow for the same binding
- Pending per-user-headers flow rows → hard-deletes just the flow

Note: pending per-user OAuth flow rows are **not** revocable by this
endpoint — they expire naturally or are cleared when the bound token
row is revoked. To cancel a pending OAuth flow, revoke its parent token
(if one exists) or wait for expiry.

Meridian does **not** call the upstream provider's revoke endpoint —
revocation is local. Per-user-headers credentials never call upstream.

post.summary: Re-authenticate or edit an MCP session
post.description:
Mints a fresh authentication flow against the same MCP client and identity
as the existing row. Two branches based on row type:

- **OAuth token** (any non-`orphaned` row, typically `needs_reauth` —
  but `active` is also accepted) — opens a fresh upstream OAuth consent
  flow. Caller is expected to follow `authorize_url` to the provider;
  on callback the credential is replaced in place.
- **Header credential** (`active` or `needs_update`) — opens a fresh
  per-user-headers submission flow. Caller follows the same URL field
  to the Meridian submission form; on submit the credential is replaced
  in place. `kind: "headers"` is set on the response.

Refused with 403 if the row is `orphaned` — a fresh credential wouldn't
help; the issue is the identity has lost access to the MCP, which the
admin must fix.

DiscoveredNode.description:
A token-verified node the ACTIVE placement does not hold — alive in gossip,
sitting in the parked-join registry, or both. Computed per request, never
persisted. A parked entry proves the token by construction (its join RPC
reached the meta leader through the cluster-token interceptor); gossip does
not, since memberlist itself is unauthenticated, so members that advertise a
different token hash are filtered out before this join and never appear here.

That filter only bites where a `cluster_token` is configured. The token is
optional and unset by default, and an unconfigured token verifies every
member — the token-less deployment, not a bypass — so without one any host
that can reach the gossip port is reported here and can be admitted in one
click. Set `cluster_token` wherever the gossip port is not on a trusted
network.

Note `drained` counts as PLACED (the node is still in the document) while
`excluded` does not. A node whose re-admission is already committed to Latest
is likewise not reported here for the duration of its convergence — the
admission is in flight, and re-adding it would rotate its identity again.

MCPHeadersFlowDetail.description:
Response for GET /api/mcp/per-user-headers/flows/{id}. Carries the schema
the end-user needs to fill in plus identity binding info for display.

required_header_keys.description: Header names the end-user must supply on this submission

admin_header_keys.description:
Names (not values) of static admin headers attached to every per-user
request. Surfaced so the user understands what context will accompany
their values.

submitted_keys.description:
Names of header keys already on the caller's existing credential.
Populated whenever a credential exists for the binding (both `active`
and `needs_update` states — `orphaned` credentials are filtered
server-side). Values are never returned. `has_active_credential` only
flips to true when the credential is in `active` state.

has_active_credential.description:
True when a credential already exists for the flow's (mode, identity,
mcp_client) triple. The submission UI uses this to render an "edit"
affordance instead of a fresh form.

MCPHeadersSubmitRequest.description:
Request body for PUT /api/mcp/per-user-headers/flows/{id}. The flow row
identifies the (mode, identity, mcp_client) triple, so the caller carries
only the values. Extra keys not in the live `per_user_header_keys` schema
are dropped server-side.

MCPOauthFlowDetail.description:
Response for GET /api/oauth/per-user/flows/{id}. Mirrors the headers-side
`MCPHeadersFlowDetail` — identity binding for display plus the bits the
consent UI needs to decide its copy.

has_active_token.description:
True when an active token already exists for the flow's binding. A
pending flow with this set means OAuth was re-initiated unnecessarily;
the consent page can render this as "already authenticated" instead
of prompting again.

MCPSessionReauthResponse.description:
Response for POST /api/mcp/sessions/{id}/reauth. Returns the URL the caller
must visit to complete the fresh authentication / resubmission.

authorize_url.description:
Where the caller must go. For OAuth rows this is the upstream provider's
authorize page (via a Meridian intermediate). For header credential rows
it's the Meridian submission form for the new flow.

submit_url.description:
Set only on header re-auth and identical to authorize_url. Kept for
callers that want to be explicit about the underlying surface.

session_id.description: ID of the freshly-minted flow row

id.description: Row primary key — token UUID, header credential UUID, or flow UUID

kind.description:
Row type:
- token: completed per-user OAuth credential
- header: completed per-user-headers credential
- flow: pending submission / consent flow (use auth_kind to disambiguate OAuth vs Headers)

auth_kind.description:
Disambiguates flow rows by which auth surface they belong to. For
`kind=token` this is always `oauth`; for `kind=header` always `headers`.

auth_mode.description: Identity dimension this credential is keyed against

user_id.description: Populated on user-keyed rows; refers to the SCIM user table

user.description: Preloaded user summary; nil when the user table is not available

status.description:
OAuth tokens use: active | orphaned | needs_reauth.
Header credentials use: active | orphaned | needs_update.
Flow rows use: pending.

expires_at.description: When the OAuth access token expires; nil for header rows

last_refreshed_at.description: OAuth token rows only — last successful refresh

updated_at.description: Header credential rows only — last submission / edit

can_reauth.description:
Mirrors the server-side identity gate on POST /api/mcp/sessions/{id}/reauth.
Always true for vk- and session-mode rows. For user-mode rows, true only
when the calling user matches the row's bound user — admin DAC scope is
enough to see the row, but reauthing mints credentials under whoever clicks
the URL, so the server returns 403 to non-bound callers. The UI hides the
Re-authenticate / Edit values action when this is false.

MeBinding.description:
A binding the subject user holds, enriched with the scope display name and
the per-scope effective permission names. On GET /api/auth/rbac/users/{user_id}
this includes bindings at scopes the CALLER cannot otherwise see — full
disclosure is the endpoint's accepted risk (authz.md 6.7).

scope_display_name.description: Human-readable name of the binding's scope entity.

permissions.description: Effective permission names granted at this scope.

MeResponse.description:
A user's identity, legacy role, and scoped bindings. Shared by
GET /api/auth/rbac/me and GET /api/auth/rbac/users/{user_id}, so the subject is
whichever user the route resolved — the caller on /me, the path parameter's
user on the profile route.

display_name.description:
The user's human-readable name; empty when unset or when no user record
resolves.

legacy_role.description:
The user's legacy role ("admin", "user_manager", "none", …); empty
when no user record resolves.

auth_source.description:
Which authority owns the account's credentials ("local" or "ldap");
empty when no user record resolves.

Migration.description: One customer migration between two shards.

age_seconds.description:
Seconds since `started_at`, frozen at `completed_at` for a terminal
migration.

stuck.description:
True when a non-terminal migration is older than the 30-minute maximum
migration age. A stuck migration is recovered with `retry` (forward) or
`abort?force=true` (backward).

MigrationConflict.description: Refusal body written by the customer-subtree mutation lock. `customer_migrating` carries the live migration's id and phase; `migration_state_unknown` is the fail-closed answer when that state could not be read, and carries `entity_id` instead.

entity_id.description: The team or virtual key whose owning customer could not be resolved.

MigrationGroup.description:
One fan-out unit of a customer migration. `team_id` is an internal grouping;
it is not an addressable migration unit — the customer is the only supported
unit. An empty `team_id` is the customer group, carrying the customer's own
budget and its customer-direct virtual keys.

team_id.description: Owning team, or `""` for the customer-direct group.

normalized_name.description: Human-readable name derived from the Meridian datasheet base model (e.g. "Claude Sonnet 4.5"). Only present when the model has a matching entry in the Meridian pricing catalog.

reasoning.description: Reasoning capabilities advertised by the provider's list-models API (e.g. OpenRouter's per-model reasoning object). Fields are omitted when the provider does not report them; supported_efforts and default_effort are absent for models whose reasoning has no selectable effort level.

model_name.description: Name of the model. Use `*` to match all models.

provider.description: Provider name (optional - applies to all providers if not specified)

scope.description: Scope where this limit applies. `global` covers all traffic; `virtual_key` scopes to a single virtual key; `user` scopes to a single user (Enterprise only).

scope_id.description: ID of the scope target (e.g. virtual key ID or user ID). Required when scope is not `global`.

scope_name.description: Resolved human-readable name of the scope target (read-only, set by server).

calendar_aligned.description: When true, all budgets reset at clean calendar boundaries (midnight UTC for day, Monday for week, 1st for month, Jan 1 for year).

budgets.description: Budget configurations for this model limit. Each entry must have a unique reset_duration.

budget.description: Deprecated: use `budgets`. Returns the first budget for backward compatibility.

rate_limit.description: Rate limit configuration for this model

created_at.description: When this model config was created

updated_at.description: When this model config was last updated

ModelConfigResponse.description: Response containing a created/updated model config

MutationResult.description:
The uniform result of a versioned mutation. Which fields are populated tells
the caller exactly how far the request got: a preview carries the plan it
WOULD run, a staged commit carries only its version, and an applied commit
carries the execution to poll.

version.description:
The committed document version — or, for a dry run, the version that
WOULD have been committed.

plan.description: The reconciliation the version implies. Present on a dry run.

execution_id.description: Handle to poll via `GET /api/cluster/v1/topology/executions/{id}`. Present when `applied` is true.

extra_headers.description: Additional headers to include in requests

insecure_skip_verify.description: Disable TLS certificate verification for provider connections. This bypasses server certificate validation and should be used only as a last resort when a trusted CA chain cannot be configured. Prefer ca_cert_pem for self-signed or private CA deployments.

ca_cert_pem.description: PEM-encoded CA certificate to trust for provider endpoint connections (e.g. self-signed or internal CA)

allow_private_network.description: Allow connections to RFC 1918 private IPs (10.x, 172.16.x, 192.168.x). Enable for providers on a k8s pod network, LAN, or private VPC. Loopback addresses (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1) remain allowed regardless of this setting. Link-local addresses (169.254.x.x) are always blocked.

Node.description:
A cluster member as declared by the topology. It carries only identity
(WHO). A node's address is never stored in consensus — it is resolved live
through the discovery chain, so a node that restarts on a new IP needs no
topology change. The node's `_meta` raft member ID is not here either: it is
the node's replica ID in the `_meta` group.

region.description:
IMMUTABLE placement label, seeded from the node's gossip metadata at
admission. Empty when the node announced no region or was admitted
before gossip converged. Changing it requires excluding and re-adding
the node — no API may set it.

labels.description: Further placement dimensions. Region is not duplicated here.

created_at.description: Stamped once, at admission.

NodeHealth.description:
Observed node liveness joined in from gossip at read time — never part of
the Document. `unknown` is reported during the pre-gossip boot window so
consumers raise no false alarms.

NodeMetrics.description:
This node's load as its meter samples it once a second: process runtime,
HTTP concurrency and status rates, budget operation rates, the per-shard
admission summaries and the last 60 seconds of all of them. Node-local —
use `?target=` to read a peer.

gc_pause_p99_ms.description: p99 over the pauses that occurred in the last sampling window, not over the process lifetime.

inflight.description: Requests inside the transport handler chain. A streaming request leaves the count when its headers are written.

unwind_queue_depth.description: Queued compensations for abandoned reservations, summed over the shards this node hosts.

history.description: The last 60 one-second buckets, oldest first.

NodeState.description:
Administrative node state. Consensus-managed and sticky: it changes only
through an explicit topology mutation, never from observed health.

- `active` — hosts replicas and receives new ones.
- `draining` — being emptied of replicas by a plan.
- `drained` — holds no replicas but is still a cluster member (reversible
  via `POST /nodes/{name}/activate`).
- `excluded` — retired. Its `_meta` member ID is never reused.

NodeStatus.description: One declared node joined with its observed health.

live_addr.description:
The node's raft gRPC address, resolved live through the discovery chain
(WHERE). Display-only — never stored in the Document — and empty when no
resolver is wired or the name is currently unresolvable.

effective_state.description:
The node's CONVERGED state, derived from the Active document — notably
`drained` for a draining node that no longer holds data-plane replicas, a
state the Document never stores. `node.state` above reports LATEST
(declared intent), so the pair reads as intent-vs-reality: equal means
converged, different means a staged or in-flight change. Falls back to the
declared state for a staged add that has not converged yet.

park.description:
Join-refusal detail for a node the document STILL places whose joiner is
nevertheless being turned away (the name fence, a stale activation, a
non-active Target state). Such a node is deliberately absent from
`discovered[]` — it already has its own entry here — so this is the only
place the refusal surfaces. Omitted when the node's join is not parked.

ObservedGroupHealth.description:
Observed availability of one raft group, joined at read time. The numeric
fields serialize as explicit JSON `null` (never a measured-looking zero)
when the observation is unavailable or not applicable.

state.description:
Monotonic observed-availability state:
- `unknown` — no observation yet (pre-gossip boot window or no source);
  numeric observations are null.
- `healthy` — every declared voter is observed alive.
- `degraded` — the group lost redundancy but retains quorum.
- `quorum_lost` — observed alive voters are below quorum (CRITICAL).

source.description:
Origin of the observation. `gossip` is deliberately not authoritative
Raft progress evidence; `none` means no health source is wired.

healthy_voters.description:
Declared voters observed alive. Explicit `null` while `state` is
`unknown`.

failure_tolerance.description:
`max(healthy_voters - quorum, 0)` — voters that may still fail before
quorum is lost. Explicit `null` while `state` is `unknown`.

below_min_replicas.description:
Data-plane placement-policy fact (`healthy_voters` is below the
effective `min_replicas`), independent of Raft availability. Always
`null` for `_meta` (not held to the placement rule) and `null` while
`state` is `unknown`.

PlacementRule.description:

TiKV-parity fields (label_constraints, location_labels, isolation_level,
role_counts, min_in_sync), each addable without a migration.

group, as an override (`Group.placement` — RESERVED/inert in v1).

The auto-repair reconciler's bounded diagnostic snapshot. Leaders report

- `standby` — a follower with nothing replicated to report.
- `idle` — converged, no action required.
- `waiting` — within the stability/cooldown window.
- `blocked` — will not proceed (staged operator intent, quorum lost,
  failed execution, or policy rejection).
- `running` — committing a repair action.
- `error` — could not read the views or sample live state.

cluster-wide aggregate.

Virtual keys whose customer_id references a customer that no longer
exists. They resolve to no shard, so only the anchor shard (shard0)
reports a non-zero value; every other shard reports 0. Visibility only —
deleting a customer is never blocked on referencing keys.

`false`) on a declared shard.

An orphan entry carries its `id` only: `replicas`, `placement` and the
timestamps are zero because there is no document to read them from, and
`GET /shards/{shard_id}` and `/shards/{shard_id}/counters` answer 404
for it. It is listable so an operator can see it, not inspectable.

reset_config.description: Window settings the reset duration cannot express. Only valid when reset_duration is quarterly (`1Q`); the API rejects it on any other window.

quarter_start_month.description: First month of Q1 as 1-12, so a fiscal year opening in April (4) gives Apr-Jun / Jul-Sep / Oct-Dec / Jan-Mar. Omitted means January. Quarter boundaries repeat every three months, so only the value modulo 3 changes the reset dates: January, April, July and October all reset on calendar quarters and differ only in which quarter is labelled Q1.

calendar_aligned.description: Set to true or false to enable or disable calendar-aligned resets. Only valid with reset durations that use day, week, month, quarter, or year suffixes (`d`, `w`, `M`, `Q`, `Y`); sub-day durations (e.g. `1h`, `30m`) are invalid with calendar alignment and the API rejects that combination. When enabling on an existing budget, alignment takes effect from the next period: the current window keeps its start and its accumulated usage, and the first aligned reset happens at the next boundary. Changing quarter_start_month on a calendar-aligned quarterly budget does not move last_reset directly; the new definition shifts where the current window starts, so the budget converges onto the new fiscal boundary on the next reset tick.

scope_type.description: Scope level of the visible scope

scope_id.description: Scope entity ID (empty for global scope)

access_type.description: Access classification at this scope (only *.admin roles are admin)

WebhookDelivery.description: One delivery attempt in an endpoint's history.

webhook_id.description: The webhook-id header value; stable across retries of the same event.

request_id.description: The async job's inference request id — the same id the LLM logs record. Empty when the job row expired before the attempt.

status_code.description: HTTP status the receiver returned, when the attempt reached it.

WebhookDeliveryOutcome.description:
Outcome of a single delivery attempt:
- delivered: the receiver returned 2xx
- retryable_failure: failed but will be retried
- permanent_failure: failed in a way that is not retried
- exhausted: retries were used up without success

WebhookEndpoint.description:
A registered webhook endpoint. The signing secret is never included in this
representation; custom header values are redacted.

additionalProperties.description:
A redacted secret-bearing value as returned in responses. The literal is
masked ("<REDACTED>"); ref and type describe the original source when set.

consecutive_failures.description: Number of consecutive failed deliveries; reset on the next success.

count.description: Number of endpoints in this page.

WebhookEndpointRequest.description:
Create or update body for a webhook endpoint. The signing secret is never
accepted here — it is generated by the server and returned once at creation,
and can only be changed through the rotate-secret endpoint.

url.description: Delivery URL. HTTPS is required unless allow_private_network is set.

additionalProperties.description:
A secret-bearing value. May be a plain string, or an object referencing an
environment variable so the literal value is never stored inline.

headers.description:
Custom headers sent with every delivery. Values support env var syntax
("env.MY_VAR") and are encrypted at rest. Reserved delivery headers
(webhook-id, webhook-timestamp, webhook-signature, content-type, etc.)
cannot be overridden.

include_response.description: Inline the job response into delivery payloads, capped by max_response_payload_kbs.

allow_private_network.description: Permit private-network receivers and plain http. Link-local and metadata addresses stay blocked.

disabled.description: Register the endpoint without delivering to it.

max_retries.description: Retries after the first failed attempt (default 4). 0 selects the default.

retry_backoff_initial_seconds.description: Delay before the first retry; each further retry doubles it (default 30). 0 selects the default.

retry_backoff_max_seconds.description: Cap on the per-retry delay (default 1800). 0 selects the default.

attempt_timeout_seconds.description: End-to-end bound for one delivery attempt (default 10). 0 selects the default.

max_response_payload_kbs.description: Cap for inlined response payloads in KB when include_response is set (default 256). 0 selects the default.

max_concurrent_deliveries.description: Concurrent in-flight deliveries to this endpoint per node (default 10). 0 selects the default.

WebhookEndpointWithSecret.description:
Returned once when an endpoint is created or its secret is rotated. The
secret is shown a single time and cannot be retrieved again.

secret.description: The signing secret in whsec_ format. Store it now; it is never returned again.

WebhookEvent.description:
A terminal async-job event a webhook endpoint can subscribe to:
- async_job.completed: an async job finished successfully
- async_job.failed: an async job finished with an error

ClusterForwardFailed.description: The ?target= node could not be reached; the forwarding hop failed.

ClusterTargetUnavailable.description: The ?target= selector could not name a live node to forward to.

CustomerMigrating.description: The customer subtree the mutation touches is being migrated between budget shards, or its migration state could not be read (fail closed). Reads are never refused; retry after the advertised delay.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the client should retry.

Forbidden.description: Forbidden — the caller lacks the required permission

AsyncJobId.name: job_id
AsyncJobId.description: The unique identifier of the async job

AsyncResultTTL.name: x-bf-async-job-result-ttl
AsyncResultTTL.description:
Time-to-live in seconds for the job result after completion. Defaults to 3600 (1 hour).
After expiry, the job result is automatically cleaned up.

AsyncWebhookEndpoint.name: x-bf-async-webhook
AsyncWebhookEndpoint.description:
Name of a registered webhook endpoint to notify when this job reaches a terminal
state (`completed` or `failed`). The endpoint must already exist and be enabled;
otherwise the submission is rejected with HTTP 400. If the endpoint is not subscribed
to the resulting event, the job still completes normally but no delivery is enqueued.
When omitted, no webhook is sent for the job and results are retrieved by polling.
See the Webhooks management API to register endpoints.

ClusterTargetNode.name: target
ClusterTargetNode.description: Route the request to the named cluster node; the forwarding middleware resolves it before the handler runs and relays the answer back.

ClusterServedBy.description: Node that actually served the request locally (X-Meridian-Served-By); differs from the addressed node when ?target= forwarded the request.

ApiKeyAuth.name: x-api-key
ApiKeyAuth.description:
API key authentication via the `x-api-key` header.
Virtual keys (prefixed with `sk-bf-`) can also be passed here.

BasicAuth.description: Basic authentication using username and password.

BearerAuth.description:
Bearer token authentication. Use your provider API key or Meridian authentication token.
Virtual keys (prefixed with `sk-bf-`) can also be passed here.

ManagementBearerAuth.description:
Management API authentication for `/api/*` endpoints. Use the `Authorization` header with `Bearer <API key>`.
Virtual keys, dashboard/user/session tokens, and `x-api-key` headers are not supported on management APIs.

SessionCookieAuth.name: token
SessionCookieAuth.description:
Dashboard session authentication via the HTTPOnly `token` cookie that is
set by `POST /api/session/login`. Used by the Meridian UI for same-origin
requests in place of an `Authorization` header. Accepted on session
endpoints (`logout`, `ws-ticket`) as an alternative to the management API key.

VirtualKeyAuth.name: x-bf-vk
VirtualKeyAuth.description:
Meridian Virtual Key for governance, routing, and access control. Supported on all inference endpoints (`/v1/*`, `/openai/*`, `/anthropic/*`, `/bedrock/*`, `/cohere/*`, `/genai/*`, `/langchain/*`, `/litellm/*`, `/pydanticai/*`, `/mcp`), not on management APIs (`/api/*`).
Example: `sk-bf-*` prefixed keys.

baseUrl.description: Base URL of your Meridian instance (e.g. https://meridian.mycompany.com)
